description: Single-panel engineering stress–strain plot for a fully austenitic 0.92C 28.8Mn-9.4Al (wt.%) low-density steel, comparing six austenite grain sizes. The y-axis is Stress (MPa), 0–1000 in 100-MPa major ticks; the x-axis is Elongation (%), 0–70 in 10% major ticks. An inset legend in the lower-right corner lists the six curves: 1.65 µm (solid black), 2.2 µm (solid grey), 8.4 µm (dashed), 12.4 µm (long-dashed), 21 µm (dotted) and 40 µm (fine dotted). Every curve shows a steep elastic rise to a yield knee (roughly 400–700 MPa), then continuous strain hardening to a broad maximum, followed by an abrupt near-vertical load drop at fracture. The finest grains (1.65 and 2.2 µm) sit highest, peaking close to the 1000 MPa gridline and failing at the shortest elongations (just past 45%); the two coarsest (21 and 40 µm) sit lowest, peaking below the 800 MPa gridline but extending to larger elongations. Intermediate 8.4 and 12.4 µm curves peak near 850–880 MPa. The figure demonstrates the classic grain-size strength–ductility trade-off in this alloy: finer austenite raises strength but lowers elongation. Numeric fracture elongations are not printed and must be read off the axis.

observations.observation: The figure is a single engineering stress–strain plot with Stress (MPa) on the y-axis (0–1000) and Elongation (%) on the x-axis (0–70).
The inset legend defines six grain-size curves: 1.65 µm (solid black), 2.2 µm (solid grey), 8.4 µm (dashed), 12.4 µm (long-dashed), 21 µm (dotted) and 40 µm (fine dotted).
The finest grain size, 1.65 µm, reaches the highest peak stress, approaching the 1000 MPa gridline, and drops abruptly at roughly 45% elongation.
The coarsest grain size, 40 µm, shows the lowest flow stress, peaking below the 800 MPa gridline, while the 21 µm curve lies just above it.
Each curve terminates in a near-vertical load drop at fracture rather than a gradual softening tail.
The two solid curves (1.65 and 2.2 µm) lie above all others throughout the strain-hardening region, showing that finer austenite grain size yields higher flow stress.
The alloy is a fully austenitic 0.92C 28.8Mn-9.4Al (wt.%) steel, according to the caption.
The cited text states grain sizes ranging from 1.65 µm to 40 µm were investigated in a 28.8Mn-9.4Al-0.92C (wt.%) alloy.
The cited text reports a classic Hall–Petch relation between grain size and yield strength and tensile strength with coefficients of 461 MPa µm^1/2 and 351 MPa µm^1/2, respectively.
The cited text states uniform elongation and total elongation increase with grain size, with saturation above a grain size of 10 µm.

subfigures.description: Single engineering stress–strain plot, Stress (MPa) vs Elongation (%), with six curves for austenite grain sizes 1.65, 2.2, 8.4, 12.4, 21 and 40 µm given in an inset legend; finer grain sizes give higher peak stress and earlier fracture, coarser ones lower stress and larger elongation.
